class.name: SecondOrderDynamics
class.brief_description: A value that follows a target like a spring and damper, for procedural motion that moves like a body.
class.description:
Second-order dynamics: the output follows a target like a mass on a spring and damper, so procedural motion starts, overshoots slightly and settles instead of moving on a straight line or a fixed-length tween. It solves [code]y + k1 y' + k2 y'' = x + k3 x'[/code] with [code]k1 = damping / (PI frequency)[/code], [code]k2 = 1 / (TAU frequency)^2[/code] and [code]k3 = response damping / (TAU frequency)[/code] (t3ssel8r, "Giving Personality to Procedural Animations using Math", 2022), stepped semi-implicitly with [code]k2[/code] raised to its stability bound, so any frame time stays stable. A step of zero time changes nothing, so paused frames hold exactly. The value can be a [float], [Vector2], [Vector3] or [Vector4]; the first value of another type restarts the system there. [codeblock] var follow = SecondOrderDynamics.new() follow.frequency = 2.0 follow.damping = 0.7 follow.reset(position)
func _process(delta): position = follow.update(delta, target.position) [/codeblock]

method.name: get_velocity
method.description: The current output's rate of change, per second.

method.name: reset
method.description: Puts the output at [param value], at rest, and makes [param value]'s type the system's.

method.name: update
method.description: Steps the system [param delta] seconds toward [param target] and returns the new output. A [param delta] of zero returns the output unchanged.

members.member: The damping ratio: below [code]1.0[/code] the output overshoots and comes back, [code]1.0[/code] is critically damped (no overshoot, fastest settle), above [code]1.0[/code] it creeps in.
The natural frequency in hertz: how fast the output responds to a change of target.
The initial response: [code]0.0[/code] eases in, above [code]1.0[/code] overshoots at the start, below [code]0.0[/code] first moves the other way (anticipation).
